summary: Open-source AI coding agent from the Qwen team that works in your terminal, editor, desktop app, browser or chat apps.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Qwen Code is an open-source AI coding agent. You run qwen in a project folder and ask it to explain, edit or build code. It also comes as a desktop app, an experimental web UI, editor integrations for VS Code, Zed and JetBrains, chat connectors, a headless mode for scripts and SDKs for TypeScript, Python and Java.
sixtySeconds.problem: Gives you an agent that can read and change your codebase from the terminal, with a choice of signing in with a Qwen subscription or using your own API key.
whoFor: Developers who want a terminal coding agent
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for an Apache-licensed coding agent with many interfaces and SDKs.
requirements: Node.js 22+ for the npm install (the standalone installer doesn't need it)
A Qwen subscription or a provider API key

overview: Install with the standalone script (Linux/macOS or Windows PowerShell), npm or Homebrew, then restart your terminal.
Open a terminal in your project and run qwen. Inside the session, run /auth and either sign in with a Qwen Plus or Pro subscription or configure a provider with an API key.
For automation, qwen -p runs headless in scripts and CI, and qwen serve exposes a daemon over HTTP. It is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Needs a subscription or paid API usage
Web UI and daemon are experimental
